inferences: This is a plausible match because Zorić's openness and landfill monitoring/drain-design experience fit the inspectorate task; it is reasoning, not a commitment.

Transfer and method risk: her evidence comes from closed landfills, a transfer station and gravel/alluvial aquifers, not an unlined yard with 3,400 mg/L COD; dual tracers add analysis burden and her PRB evidence covers ammonium, not bulk COD.
The proposal is conditional: Zorić's availability for the 2024 120-day window is unknown, and company technician time, site access and data sharing are not confirmed.
proposedActions: First experiment: a four-well baseline/seasonal-screening campaign at the yard, using the 1993 sketch and company COD bench data as baseline, subject to confirming site access, technician time and data sharing. Researcher contribution proposed: define well locations/depths and sampling protocol; company contribution proposed: access, records and technician support if confirmed. Measure water level, chloride, ammonium, COD and electrical conductivity at each well and selected depths, with a seasonal repeat if possible. Compare conservative chloride with reactive ammonium to test whether published closed-landfill/transfer-station assumptions hold for this unlined yard at 3,400 mg/L COD. Go/no-go: proceed only if the inspectorate confirms written well/proposal criteria in weeks 1-2, the wells give interpretable flow direction, and at least one consistent tracer signal appears; otherwise escalate. Success criteria: four interpretable wells and a defensible flow-direction map by week 12; draft remediation proposal by late June 2024. Timeline: weeks 1-2 design/permits, weeks 3-8 drilling/sampling, weeks 9-16 interpretation/draft.

Proposed next step: design the four-well network (locations, depths, screen intervals, sampling frequency) to the inspectorate's format, using first-campaign data and Zorić's dual-tracer experience; review before final drilling if flow direction remains undefined.

Draft a containment/remediation proposal comparing passive interceptor drain charts with source control, liner repair and ammonium PRB polishing; include seasonal water-table design and geochemical attenuation factors; treat PRB evidence as ammonium-only and require a COD-treatment pilot before claiming 3,400 mg/L COD treatment.

Set up a joint inspectorate/company review to confirm acceptance criteria, QA/QC, sample custody, publication and IP terms; use the company wet-chemistry bench for COD/conductivity and external lab for chloride/ammonium if budget is confirmed.

# Groundwater monitoring and leachate containment for Zelena Petlja's unlined yard

## Verified facts
- Company sampling returned COD 3,400 mg/L, above the formal-response threshold, and the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate ordered four groundwater wells within 120 days plus a remediation proposal before late June 2024. [F1]
- Only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch exists; the company does not know contamination extent or seasonal groundwater flow direction. [F2]
- The yard liner was never designed for liquid retention; a 50 mm defect increased cumulative groundwater loading by 340% relative to an intact liner under wet antecedent conditions in a published simulation. [F3]
- The company reports no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond a basic wet-chemistry bench, and two process technicians who track sorting-line performance data daily. [F4]
- Vojvodina evidence indicates mean-annual-only containment design may underestimate peak leachate infiltration by up to 40% in this climatic setting. [F5]
- Site-specific geochemical attenuation factors are expected in Serbian landfill permit risk assessments. [F6]
- Zorić is open to contract research on site-specific leachate transport modelling and containment design. [F7]
- Her field study used an 18-piezometer network over 30 months and recommends dual-tracer campaigns for comparable compliance monitoring. [F8]

## Our inference
- This is a plausible match because Zorić's openness and landfill monitoring/drain-design experience fit the inspectorate task; it is reasoning, not a commitment.
- Transfer and method risk: her evidence comes from closed landfills, a transfer station and gravel/alluvial aquifers, not an unlined yard with 3,400 mg/L COD; dual tracers add analysis burden and her PRB evidence covers ammonium, not bulk COD.
- The proposal is conditional: Zorić's availability for the 2024 120-day window is unknown, and company technician time, site access and data sharing are not confirmed.

## Proposed next steps
- First experiment: a four-well baseline/seasonal-screening campaign at the yard, using the 1993 sketch and company COD bench data as baseline, subject to confirming site access, technician time and data sharing. Researcher contribution proposed: define well locations/depths and sampling protocol; company contribution proposed: access, records and technician support if confirmed. Measure water level, chloride, ammonium, COD and electrical conductivity at each well and selected depths, with a seasonal repeat if possible. Compare conservative chloride with reactive ammonium to test whether published closed-landfill/transfer-station assumptions hold for this unlined yard at 3,400 mg/L COD. Go/no-go: proceed only if the inspectorate confirms written well/proposal criteria in weeks 1-2, the wells give interpretable flow direction, and at least one consistent tracer signal appears; otherwise escalate. Success criteria: four interpretable wells and a defensible flow-direction map by week 12; draft remediation proposal by late June 2024. Timeline: weeks 1-2 design/permits, weeks 3-8 drilling/sampling, weeks 9-16 interpretation/draft.
- Proposed next step: design the four-well network (locations, depths, screen intervals, sampling frequency) to the inspectorate's format, using first-campaign data and Zorić's dual-tracer experience; review before final drilling if flow direction remains undefined.
- Draft a containment/remediation proposal comparing passive interceptor drain charts with source control, liner repair and ammonium PRB polishing; include seasonal water-table design and geochemical attenuation factors; treat PRB evidence as ammonium-only and require a COD-treatment pilot before claiming 3,400 mg/L COD treatment.
- Set up a joint inspectorate/company review to confirm acceptance criteria, QA/QC, sample custody, publication and IP terms; use the company wet-chemistry bench for COD/conductivity and external lab for chloride/ammonium if budget is confirmed.

## Open questions
- Can Zorić confirm availability and field capacity for the 120-day window ending late June 2024, given teaching and project commitments?
- What exactly does the inspectorate require for the four wells (locations, depths, construction, sampling frequency) and what remediation-proposal format or standards will be accepted?
- What existing data can the company share: 1993 sketch, borehole logs, water levels, leachate sampling QA/QC, waste composition, yard drainage, liner condition, topography and leachate flow/volume/chemistry?
- What budget and procurement route exist for drilling, laboratory analyses and any treatment pilot, and can external funding fit the 120-day deadline?
- Will the company provide site access, technician time and permission for data use or publication, and what IP terms apply?
